questions.markdown: A Germanium diode carries a current of $10\mathrm{mA}$ under a forward bias voltage of $0.3\mathrm{V}$ at $27^\circ\mathrm{C}$. If the reverse saturation current is $4.38\mu\mathrm{A}$, find the dynamic forward resistance at $40^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

Determine the range of input voltage to obtain an output voltage of $6.3\mathrm{V}$ in a Zener voltage regulator circuit. The current flowing through Zener diode ranges from $2\mathrm{mA}$ to $28\mathrm{mA}$ and the load resistance is $1\mathrm{K}\Omega$. Assume $R_s=470\Omega$. Draw the circuit diagram.

questions.markdown:
Explain the working of a square wave generator using OP-AMP.  
In this circuit if all the resistors are $10\mathrm{K}\Omega$, $C=0.1\mu\mathrm{F}$ and $\pm V_{sat}=12\mathrm{V}$, determine the frequency of oscillation of the output square wave signal

i) With relevant circuit diagram and equations, explain the working of an OPAMP integrator.  
ii) Given three input voltage sources $V_1=1\mathrm{V}$, $V_2=\sin(wt)$ and $V_3=\cos(wt)$, design a two stage OPAMP circuit to obtain $V_0=10+5\mathrm{Sin}(wt)-5\cos(wt)$. Assume feedback resistor to be used $R_F=10\mathrm{K}\Omega$.

(i) Convert $(0101)_2$ into Gray Code.  
(ii) Perform $(45.75)_{10}-(87.75)_{10}$ subtraction using 1's complement method.

(i) Encrypt the data 1001 using $(7,4)$ even parity bit Hamming code.  
(ii) Consider a new message encrypted as "1110110" using $(7,4)$ even parity bit Hamming code transmitted through a noisy channel. Decode the message, assuming that there can be maximum of one bit error in the encrypted message received.
Solve $F=\Sigma(1,5,6,12,13,14)+d(2,4)$ using K-Map and implement resultant expression using only NAND gates.

A logic system has 3 inputs and one output, the output of the system is low only when any two of the inputs are high. Write the truth table and standard SOP. Also implement the system using basic gates.
Draw the logic diagram of a 3-bit ripple down-counter using the positive edge-triggered T flip flops. Plot the timing diagram for the same.

Design a 4-bit Serial-In Serial-Out (SISO) shift register using D flip-flops.  
(a) Draw the logic diagram showing how the flip-flops are connected.  
(b) If the input data sequence is 1101, show the contents of each flip-flop $(Q_3\ Q_2\ Q_1\ Q_0)$ after every clock pulse.  
(c) How many clock pulses are required for the entire data to appear at the output of the register?
Compare the operation of SR, JK, D, and T flip-flops in terms of input conditions, and invalid states.
Simplify and implement $F(A,B,C)=A'\ B'\ C + A\ B'\ C' + A\ B'\ C$ using an 4:1 MUX.
